objective: Finish the native Cognito password reset the frontend already ships: a static verify reminder, one generic answer for every address, Confirm password on reset and sign-up, sign-out before recovery, and an Account details entry point. Frontend only.
acceptance_criteria: Scope (ADR 0035, Prompts/22 'Reset: native Cognito only'): the browser keeps calling Cognito ForgotPassword and ConfirmForgotPassword directly through AuthService, with the code Cognito emails to the account's verified address. No backend route, migration, SES, custom sender, custom reset token or link, post-reset email, password history, paid Cognito plan, timer unlock, revocation or reset-evidence machinery. Locally verified ID tokens cannot detect a provider-side revocation: that stays a documented limit, and USERS-009's fencing covers deletion.
Test-first: the failing tests and frontend/src/test/bundle-budgets/AUTH-001.ts are committed alone; the implementation commit edits no test.
Sign-in keeps its forgot-password link below the password field, and its accessible name contains 'Forgot'.

The request step has a labelled Email input, a Send code button and, before any submission, a static reminder in the page text: a reset code goes only to a verified email address, so an account that never verified its email cannot reset its password this way. The reminder is plain text, not an alert, and is shown whatever is typed.

Every syntactically valid address gets the same next step and the same message: if an account with that verified address exists, a code has been sent. A Cognito success, UserNotFoundException and InvalidParameterException after the input passed the page's own syntax check all lead to it. No copy names an account's existence, verification state or delivery. LimitExceededException and TooManyRequestsException show one generic 'too many attempts' alert. A syntactically invalid address is a field error and makes no Cognito call. The current 'There is no account for this email address.' message is removed.

The code step has labelled Confirmation code, New password and Confirm password inputs. When New password and Confirm password differ, Confirm password shows an accessible field error (aria-invalid and a description) and no confirmForgotPassword call is made; matching values make exactly one. CodeMismatch, ExpiredCode and InvalidPassword keep their field errors, and none names account details.

Sign-up has labelled Password and Confirm password inputs. A mismatch is an accessible field error on Confirm password and makes no signUp call; matching values make exactly one. Optional email verification is unchanged.

A signed-in visitor who reaches /forgot-password is signed out (AuthContext's signOut, so the session is cleared everywhere) before the request form renders, and while AuthContext's status is still 'loading' the form does not render either. A test proves no forgotPassword call can happen while a session exists: the form is not in the document until the session is null.

Account settings begins with an Account details section (an h2 'Account details'), before 'Verify this account'. It has an Email row showing the signed-in session's email and a Password row with a Reset password control (no password value shown) that goes to /forgot-password, which then signs the user out as above.

Codes and passwords are never logged, stored outside component state or put in a URL: `no-secret-leak.test.tsx` covers the new Confirm password inputs and fails if either value reaches console output, storage or `location`.
Every new target is at least 24 by 24 CSS px and buttons keep the existing 44 px Button. Light and dark themes use existing tokens only; no new colour.
frontend/src/test/bundle-budgets/AUTH-001.ts declares every output the unit changes. Entry growth is at most 1 KiB gzip and 2 KiB raw, and no output reaches 500,000 raw bytes.
No new dependency: `frontend/package.json` is unchanged, and no new third-party origin is requested.

wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x08b-frontend-auth.md records the reset flow, the generic answer, the verify reminder, the pre-recovery sign-out and the token-revocation limit; 0x08k-frontend-account.md records Account details. 0x01b-users-auth.md states that reset is native Cognito with no backend route.

Browser rows (Director, after merge, ports 5230-5239, dev pool only): the reminder; unknown and known addresses give the same screen; mismatch errors on reset and sign-up; signed-in visit signs out; Account details at 360 and 1280. A real reset needs the emailed code: without it, that row is NOT DONE, never faked.
